The 10% bootstrap CIs include 1.0 (T=0.25 [0.837,1.134]; T=0.5 [0.980,1.210]). Claim 3: the kill and supported conditions both fire. L5c's reward-model proxy has an AUC gain of +0.003 and ratio 1.237, a different proxy from E01. L3b (2.09) and L5c's judge3b (1.67) have ratios of at least 1.5. The ratio dilutes to about 1.1 over all accepted groups. Conflicting evidence, so open. The ledger's standing view is "not supported", so W2 and W3 are false.

Claim 2: L2a compares the warm-started learner with the label-free agreement threshold (no free labels) at an equal 10% budget. The CI includes 1.0 at both temperatures, [0.837,1.134] and [0.980,1.210]. L7a finds no learner edge over the fixed-rule set. Claim 3: L3b (non-E01, judge proxy) has a neighbor ratio of 2.09 against a null p95 of 1.41, and L5c judge3b has 1.67, both at least 1.5. So "supported" holds by the rule and the kill condition fails, even though the AUC gain is only +0.007. W2 and W3 are false: the ledger concludes "not supported" for both claims, and the threshold comparison is a completed, controlled one.

Claim 2: L2a compares the warm learner with the label-free agreement threshold at the same budget (K=1, no free labels). The 95% CIs include 1.0 at both T=0.25 [0.837, 1.134] and T=0.5 [0.980, 1.210]. L7a repeats this against a larger fixed-rule set with the same result. This meets not_supported, and the free-label confound is controlled, so W2 is false. Claim 3: L3b (judge proxy) has a neighbor ratio of 2.09, and L5c judge3b has 1.67. Both are at or above 1.5 in non-E01 entries, so this is supported by the rule even though the AUC gains are small. The kill needs a ratio below 1.5, and the ratio is cut-dependent. The ledger itself says "not supported", so W3 is false.
